note: The whole-document lookups the browser half still makes outside the modules that own them, one entry per file: what it counts, when those reads happen where that is known, and which of them are debt. A lookup in a refresh pass or a frame callback costs the page's own size on every frame of a long conversation, so the sanctioned readers are the engine host.ts's accessors (cacheFirstMatch caches a match and a miss until the page's structure changes), the engine bus.ts's observeMatches registry and the engine stylesheet.ts's own sheet; every other site is recorded here and the list only shrinks. A read by an element's id is not counted: the browser answers it from its own index rather than by walking the tree. An entry whose count reaches zero comes out of the file. A unit test stands outside the rule: its document runs in the test browser and costs no reader anything.
